tasks.spec:
You are a READ-ONLY adversarial reviewer. You own exactly one output file, named at the end. Read anything named here; write nothing else. No commits, no sends, no skills, no MCP, no git mutations.

SUBJECT: wave 2 of the OBE podcast loop-drive contract, landed today at podcast commit 65cabee on branch feat/one-true-master. Two files:
  1. server/pipeline/guest_outreach_draft.py (NEW) — creates at most one gate-cleared Gmail draft for the guest-acquisition loop.
  2. scripts/run_podcast_loop.sh — the loop runner, which now invokes that module after cross-model QA passes.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL REVIEW. This repository sends real email. Two services are live: a bridge that turns podcast Gmail drafts into approval cards every 30 minutes (--execute), and an approved-send executor that SENDS every 10 minutes (--execute) and, for the class podcast_outreach_qa_passed, sends WITHOUT any human approval under an owner promotion. A Gmail draft that this module creates and that passes the bridge's QA chain WILL reach a real person. A defect here is a wrong letter sent to a prospective podcast guest.

HISTORY YOU SHOULD USE. Nine consecutive rounds of this job passed their executed check and were still rejected in review, every time for a defect the FIX invented that a check written from the DEFECT could not see. Read /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/REVIEW-r10-wave2.md for the four findings from the previous attempt. A fifth was caught while landing: the previous CLI never ran the producer at all — it read a receipt file and mapped its status, and it rejected the --ledger flag the runner passes, so every real invocation would have died on an argparse usage error whose exit code (2) is indistinguishable from 'clean stop'. The coordinator wrote the replacement main() himself, which is exactly why an independent pass is needed: nobody has reviewed that code.

HUNT LIST, in priority order:
1. main() in guest_outreach_draft.py. It constructs services, wires gates, and honors PLACEHOLDER_MODE. Is there ANY path where it creates a real Gmail draft when it should not, or reports success without one? What happens when --candidates is absent, empty, malformed, or contains a non-dict? What happens when PLACEHOLDER_MODE is set to '0' or empty string (note: os.environ.get returns a truthy '0' string)? Check that one specifically.
2. The voice gate wiring. On a live run it shells out to scripts/obe_draft_voice_qa.py. If that script is missing, times out, or prints something unparseable, what verdict does the module compute, and does an unparseable result ever become 'pass'? A draft that survives an unreadable voice gate is a letter nobody approved.
3. The gate runner. It shells out to server.pipeline.prose_gates. What if the subprocess itself fails to start (exit 3, missing module, PYTHONPATH wrong)? Does that become a block, or does it slip through?
4. Ceiling enforcement. The counts default to 0 and nothing feeds them yet — the coordinator documented this as a known gap. Verify that is the ONLY gap: is the comparison logic itself correct (>= vs >), and can a non-integer or None count reach it?
5. The runner wiring in run_podcast_loop.sh. Find the guest-acquisition branch. Confirm it sits INSIDE the QA: PASS case and AFTER the re-entry loop, that it does not introduce an exit that preempts the runner's existing exit paths, that it passes --reentry "$REENTRY_ATTEMPT" (not a hardcoded 0), and that its rc-2 escalation contains no email address, no raw draft or contact id, and no letter body. Trace the shell control flow by reading, and say plainly if you cannot determine reachability by reading alone.
6. Anything that leaks: receipts are pasted into Telegram. Grep the module for paths where a recipient address, a draft id, or body text could reach the receipt or the escalation.

You may run read-only commands (grep, sed -n, python3 -m py_compile, git log/show/diff). You may execute the module's own check at /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u2a_producer_check.py --repo /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast --module-only --out /tmp/r12-review — it is safe and touches no provider. Do NOT run scripts/run_podcast_loop.sh.

OUTPUT (mandatory): write /mnt/d_drive/ringer-work/loop-drive-contract-r12/wave2-review.md — FIRST LINE exactly 'QA: PASS' or 'QA: REVISE' or 'QA: BLOCK', then findings most severe first, each with a file:line citation and the concrete input that triggers it. QA: PASS only if you would bet a live send on this code tonight.
tasks.check: bash -c 'head -1 /mnt/d_drive/ringer-work/loop-drive-contract-r12/wave2-review.md 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^QA: (PASS|REVISE|BLOCK)$" || { echo "CHECK FAIL: no verdict line"; exit 1; }; grep -cE "[a-z_]+\.(py|sh):[0-9]+" /mnt/d_drive/ringer-work/loop-drive-contract-r12/wave2-review.md | awk "{ if (\$1<2) { print \"CHECK FAIL: fewer than 2 file:line citations\"; exit 1 } else print \"CHECK PASS: verdict plus citations\" }"'
tasks.verified: an independent model reviewed the coordinator's own main() and the landed wiring against a live-send threat model, with file:line evidence
